chapter: Massey Hall, race and the record business
title: Not evil, paranoid: police in the ghettos
summary: Asked what posterity should know, Mingus talks of being called Evil by Jimmy Rowles, ghetto police and the beating of Max Roach.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Anything you'd like to say, Charles? What would you like posterity to know about you?
I went to Brownie's the other night, to hear Jimmy Rowles. And he came up to the piano and
said, "Evil --" He called me Evil. You were there. I wonder where he read that, because I've never even raised my voice at him. (Inaudible) dropped our friendship, at least, I did.
Yeah, I wondered what had happened.

I'm not evil, man. I'm paranoid. I think the white man is against the black man. I think the police in the ghettos and the yellows should be mostly black, because, like, in the Jewish neighborhoods they have Jewish policemen. And in the Irish neighborhood they have Irish policemen. In an Italian neighborhood they have Italian policemen. The ghetto police are all white. Two or three black guys go down to a police station, they're afraid to say anything.

I speak from experience, because I saw them beating Max Roach up in a jail house. He was drunk, and they were beating him like he was a criminal or something. So I went and told them let him alone and who he was. They started beating on me, man. So I'd like to go down in history as and all saying my little funny song titles that were purposely done to tell what a phony country this is, with -- as far as their pretense to be -- to feel that black people are equal to the white people, let alone to the Japanese or the Chinese or any minority.
They're starting to kill the Puerto Ricans now, too, the same way. That's what I'd like to go down saying, man.
